5_coverage.route_differences: (1) Order of results: the Lean project constructs a PERIODIC viscosity-one candidate first (ActualCandidateAssembly.selected_candidate proving ProblemStatement.candidateStatement) and derives alternative (D) from periodic uniqueness/maximal lifespan; the whole-space alternative (C) is then obtained by extracting the compactly supported fields behind the periodisation (R3CompactCandidate.of_localized_fields) and applying whole-space finite-energy uniqueness. The paper proves Theorem 1.1 on R^3 first and obtains Corollary 10.6 by rescaling into the fundamental cube and periodising. (2) There is no Lean counterpart of the local-field theorem (Theorem 3.1) on Omega_* as a separate statement: MixedCandidateAssembly.candidate_of_finite_stages goes from finite correction stages directly to CandidateProperties, folding Proposition 9.9, Proposition 10.1 (cut potential before curl, direct angular field cut separately, time switch), Lemma 10.2 (joint jet limits) and Lemma 10.3 (Borel extension) into one assembly; the inner growth (3.6)/(10.21) is used only as unbounded speed (Tendsto atTop), not as an asymptotic rate. (3) Viscosity is fixed to one throughout the construction and restored by the scaling in ComparatorBridge (force nu^2 f(nu t, x)), essentially the paper's (10.22). (4) Lemma 10.5 (weak-strong uniqueness without growth assumptions on the competitor's pressure) is proved by a full pressure-recovery/Riesz-commutator argument (NavierStokes/R3/) rather than the paper's short energy argument. (5) The Lean cites a "candidate manuscript" with different numbering (Part I periodic with sections 3-11 and Appendix A; "Part II" whole space), so the Lean was written against an earlier draft; intermediate statements are organised by construction stage (nominal profile Witness structures, correction-cycle Invariant records, weighted classes on StripData) rather than by the paper's lemma list, and many paper lemmas correspond to several Lean declarations (see match_form).
beyond_the_79: Clay-form top-level theorems NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 and navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic (ComparatorSolution.lean), stated with the Formal-Conjectures reference definitions (InitialVelocityConditionDecay/Periodic, ForceConditionDecay/Periodic, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn/Periodic) copied in ComparatorDefinitions.lean; ComparatorBridge/ComparatorR3Bridge translate operators, rescale viscosity (a viscosity-one candidate is rescaled to every nu>0) and normalise a hypothetical global solution back to viscosity one.

The periodic viscosity-one target NavierStokes.ProblemStatement.candidateStatement/CandidateProperties (smooth, unit-periodic, zero datum, compact future time support of the force, exact PDE on (0,1), SpeedUnboundedAtOne) and its proof ActualCandidateAssembly.selected_candidate; the periodic route (D) via PeriodicUniqueness.classical_uniqueness_on_Icc, PeriodicSobolev (concrete H^3 sup bound), MaximalLifespan (maximal classical lifespan exactly one, candidate_excludes_global_solution), CandidateConsequences (force jet decay) and CompactForceDecay.

R3CompactCandidate: extraction of the compact whole-space fields "behind the periodic construction" (cut potential, direct field and pressure before periodisation, second larger cutoff for the force), then R3FiniteEnergyComparison.

Whole-space finite-energy uniqueness machinery under NavierStokes/R3/ (about 70 modules, all in the closure): pressure recovery for smooth finite-energy competitors via Schwartz/Fourier pairings, double Riesz transforms with heat-kernel representation, cutoff commutator with an L^(4/3) radial majorant, weighted Sobolev/Young/Gronwall closure, WholeSpaceEnergyLimit. The paper's Lemma 10.5 is a short lemma; the Lean proof is a large independent development.

Arithmetic and geometry checks not in the paper as statements: ExponentLedger (kappa=10^-5 admissibility, stage arithmetic), ActualIterationLedger (explicit gain/accuracy sequences), DiophantineGraph (Diophantine bounds for the graph directions (1,1-sqrt2),(sqrt2-1,1)), SlotColoring (an explicit 2250-colour proper colouring of the physical grid labels), Scaling (Reynolds-number scaling of core and carrier; cites "Proposition A.2 and Remark 8.6"), BlowupImplication (abstract inference that a nonzero profile with negative time power forces unbounded speed and no continuous extension; cites "Proposition 11.7").
